mcq.explanation: Helm is a package manager for Kubernetes: it bundles related manifests into a versioned chart and installs, upgrades and rolls them back as a single release.
mcq.distractors: Container runtimes (containerd, CRI-O), network protocols and hypervisors live at lower layers; Helm only talks to the Kubernetes API.

mcq.explanation: A Helm chart is a package of Kubernetes templates and metadata: a directory (or .tgz) with Chart.yaml, values.yaml and a templates/ folder that Helm renders into manifests.
mcq.distractors: A running Pod is what a chart eventually creates, not the chart itself; disks and Git branches are unrelated.

mcq.explanation: Chart.yaml holds chart metadata such as name and version (plus apiVersion: v2, appVersion, description, dependencies).
mcq.distractors: Logs, certificates and Terraform state are never stored in Chart.yaml.

mcq.explanation: values.yaml supplies the default configurable values for templates; templates read them as `.Values.<key>` and users override them with -f or --set.
mcq.distractors: Registry credentials can be passed as values, but that is not its purpose, and Git history and PIDs have nothing to do with it.

mcq.explanation: `helm create <name>` scaffolds a starter chart with Chart.yaml, values.yaml, templates/ (Deployment, Service, Ingress, helpers) and .helmignore.
mcq.distractors: `helm init` existed only in Helm 2 (to install Tiller) and never created charts; the other commands do not exist.

mcq.explanation: `helm install <release> <chart>` renders the chart and creates a new named release in the cluster.
mcq.distractors: Helm has no `apply` or `deploy` subcommand (that is kubectl/other tools); `helm push` uploads a packaged chart to an OCI registry.

mcq.explanation: `helm upgrade <release> <chart>` applies a new chart version or new values to an existing release and records a new revision (`--install` creates it if missing).
mcq.distractors: There is no `helm restart`, `helm rerun` or `helm patch`; rolling Pods is done by upgrading or with kubectl rollout restart.

mcq.explanation: `helm rollback <release> [revision]` returns a release to an earlier revision; with no revision number it goes to the previous one, and it records a new revision number.
mcq.distractors: Helm has no revert, reset or undo subcommands; `kubectl rollout undo` is the kubectl equivalent for a single Deployment.

mcq.explanation: `--set key=value` overrides a single value on the command line (e.g. `--set replicaCount=3`), taking precedence over values.yaml and -f files.
mcq.distractors: The other flags do not exist in Helm; port-forward is a kubectl command.

mcq.explanation: `helm template` renders the chart templates locally and prints the manifests without installing anything (useful for review or piping into kubectl diff).
mcq.distractors: `helm install --dry-run` is the other way to preview; the listed alternatives are not real Helm commands.

checks.label: Explains the templates directory (manifests rendered with values)

labs.modelAnswer:
helm create webapp
# webapp/
#   Chart.yaml        chart metadata: apiVersion v2, name, version (chart version), appVersion, description
#   values.yaml       default configurable values that templates read via .Values; overridden with -f or --set
#   templates/        Kubernetes manifests written as Go templates; Helm renders them with the values into real YAML
#   charts/           packaged dependency charts (subcharts)

# webapp/Chart.yaml
apiVersion: v2
name: webapp
description: A simple web application
type: application
version: 0.1.0
appVersion: "1.27"

# webapp/values.yaml
replicaCount: 2
image:
  repository: nginx
  tag: "1.27"
service:
  type: ClusterIP
  port: 80

# webapp/templates/deployment.yaml (excerpt)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-webapp
spec:
  replicas: {{ .Values.replicaCount }}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: {{ .Release.Name }}-webapp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: {{ .Release.Name }}-webapp
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: "{{ .Values.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.image.tag }}"
          ports:
            - containerPort: 80

helm lint webapp
helm template demo webapp   # render manifests locally to check them
labs.explanation: Tests whether you know a chart's anatomy. Chart.yaml is metadata (name, chart version, appVersion), values.yaml holds the defaults, and templates/ contains Go-templated manifests that reference `.Values`, `.Release` and `.Chart`. Check that `helm lint` passes and that `helm template` renders valid YAML.

checks.label: Renders templates to verify (helm template / --dry-run / get manifest)
Verifies installed resources (kubectl get / helm status)

labs.modelAnswer:
# templates/service.yaml uses the port value
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: {{ .Release.Name }}-webapp
spec:
  type: {{ .Values.service.type }}
  selector:
    app: {{ .Release.Name }}-webapp
  ports:
    - port: {{ .Values.service.port }}
      targetPort: 80

# Render first to check the output
helm template web ./webapp --set image.repository=nginx --set image.tag=1.27 --set replicaCount=3 --set service.port=8080

# Install with the overrides
helm install web ./webapp -n demo --create-namespace \
  --set image.repository=nginx \
  --set image.tag=1.27 \
  --set replicaCount=3 \
  --set service.port=8080

# Verify
helm list -n demo
helm get manifest web -n demo
helm get values web -n demo
kubectl get deploy,svc,pods -n demo
kubectl get deploy web-webapp -n demo -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}'
labs.explanation: Tests parameterising a chart and checking what was actually deployed. The image, replicas and Service port must come from `.Values` so `--set` or a values file changes them. Verify both the rendered output (`helm template` or `helm get manifest`) and the live objects (`kubectl get deploy,svc`): 3 ready replicas, the right image, Service on port 8080.

checks.label: Checks final status (helm status / helm list)

labs.modelAnswer:
# Revision 1 already exists from helm install
helm upgrade web ./webapp -n demo --reuse-values --set image.tag=1.27.2 --set replicaCount=4
helm history web -n demo
# REVISION  STATUS      DESCRIPTION
# 1         superseded  Install complete
# 2         deployed    Upgrade complete

helm rollback web 1 -n demo   # or omit 1 to go back to the previous revision
helm history web -n demo      # rollback is recorded as new revision 3 (deployed), copying revision 1's config
helm status web -n demo
kubectl get deploy -n demo -o wide
labs.explanation: Tests the release lifecycle. Every install, upgrade or rollback creates a new revision, so after rolling back, `helm history` shows revision 3 with the description 'Rollback to 1', not a return to revision 1. Confirm with `helm status` (STATUS: deployed) and that the Deployment's image and replicas match the original values again.
